chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Al-Hakam ibn Maskin, from Jamil and Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the child of a free man and a slave-girl, he said: The child follows the free parent.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a child born to a free man and a slave woman in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this chain to establish the principle of 'taliq' (attachment), where a child born to a free man and a slave woman follows the status of the free parent. This ruling, attributed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), ensures the child inherits the higher social and legal standing of the free parent, a key distinction in Shia fiqh regarding lineage and inheritance. The hadith underscores the importance of the father's status in determining the child's freedom, reflecting the juristic consensus on the maternal bond in cases of mixed-status unions.
